overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating outside a posted meeting via emails on a letter, but found no intentional violation and declined to review the notice-sufficiency allegation.

allegations.summary: Board members allegedly deliberated outside a posted meeting by drafting, circulating and revising a letter responding to Executive Order 14238 by email.
allegations.key_passage: As such, the letter constituted deliberation and should have been discussed in an open meeting.

allegations.summary: The Board argued it did not violate the law because the topic was discussed at the April 9 meeting and a vote to prepare a letter was taken there.
allegations.key_passage: It does not list as an exception a topic that has already been discussed at a meeting.

allegations.summary: Chair's one-way email asking members to send input only to her and the Director was alleged to be a further deliberation problem.
allegations.key_passage: The Board ran afoul of the Open Meeting Law when the letter was circulated to a quorum of members; a response was not required for there to be a violation.

allegations.summary: Complainant asked that the Board be found to have acted intentionally in violating the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: We do not find this violation to be intentional.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged insufficient notice for the outside-meeting deliberations on specified dates in May.
allegations.key_passage: Insufficiency of notice is subsumed by the main allegation of the complaint, that deliberations occurred outside a properly posted meeting.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Release of any written communication, including emails, between or among a quorum of Board members about the letter issued in response to Executive Order 14238.
Certify to the AG's office within forty-five (45) days of the letter's date that the release has been done.
